This is a well-structured, accessible HTML5 document demonstrating modern best practices for semantic markup and inclusive design.

It uses semantic landmarks, a skip link for keyboard navigation, and CSS that adapts to your light or dark mode preference.

Text and link colors meet WCAG AA contrast in both themes, type scales with your browser's font size, and motion respects your system settings.

Features

  • Semantic HTML structure with proper landmarks
  • Keyboard accessible navigation and focus management
  • Dark mode support with custom color schemes
  • Responsive typography using modern CSS
  • Print-friendly styles for better readability
  • WCAG AA contrast compliance in all color modes

Examples

Component Cards

Card components are useful for organizing related content. They include a subtle border and padding for visual separation.

Learn more about accessibility resources

Interactive Elements

Buttons and links are fully accessible with clear focus states. All interactive elements include visible focus indicators and proper ARIA labels.

Keyboard navigation: Use Tab to move forward, Shift+Tab to move backward, and Enter to activate.

Fields marked * are required.

For example, name@example.com

input.new_string:
<script>
		const themeToggle = document.getElementById('theme-toggle');
		const htmlElement = document.documentElement;
		const prefersDark = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)');

		const updateThemeUI = () => {
			const isDark = htmlElement.style.colorScheme === 'dark' ||
				(!htmlElement.style.colorScheme && prefersDark.matches);
			themeToggle.textContent = isDark ? '☀️' : '🌙';
			themeToggle.setAttribute('aria-label', isDark ? 'Switch to light mode' : 'Switch to dark mode');
		};

		if (themeToggle) {
			const stored = localStorage.getItem('theme');
			if (stored) {
				htmlElement.style.colorScheme = stored;
				updateThemeUI();
			}

			themeToggle.addEventListener('click', () => {
				const current = htmlElement.style.colorScheme || (prefersDark.matches ? 'dark' : 'light');
				const next = current === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark';
				htmlElement.style.colorScheme = next;
				localStorage.setItem('theme', next);
				updateThemeUI();
			});

			prefersDark.addEventListener('change', () => {
				if (!localStorage.getItem('theme')) {
					updateThemeUI();
				}
			});
		}

		const copyrightYear = document.getElementById('copyright-year');
		if (copyrightYear) {
			copyrightYear.textContent = String(new Date().getFullYear());
		}

Perfect! I've made several meaningful improvements to your HTML document:

## Key Improvements:

1. **Fixed JSON-LD Schema** - Changed author from email to proper name "K. Smith"

2. **Theme Toggle Button** - Added an interactive dark/light mode switcher in the header with:
   - Visual emoji indicator (🌙 moon for light mode, ☀️ sun for dark mode)
   - LocalStorage persistence (remembers user preference)
   - Accessible ARIA labels that update dynamically
   - Respects system preference changes

3. **Accessibility Features Section** - Added a new section with:
   - Properly structured `<table>` with semantic elements
   - `<caption>` for table description
   - `<thead>` and `<tbody>` for proper structure
   - `scope="col"` and `scope="row"` attributes for header associations
   - Example data showing browser feature support
   - This demonstrates accessible table best practices to screen readers

4. **Updated Navigation** - Added link to new Accessibility Features section

5. **Additional Resource** - Added MDN Web Accessibility link to resources

All improvements maintain the document's strong accessibility foundation and CSS doesn't need changes since it already supports the theme toggle through CSS variables. The document is now ready to test with a browser!
